(also mānāpya, q.v.; = Pali mānatta), a kind of penance which is superimposed, after parivāsa, on a monk guilty of a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense which he has concealed: bhikṣuṇā … mānatvaṃ (12) caritavyaṃ bhavati, cīrṇa-mānatvo (after he has undergone the m˚) bhikṣur …; for mānāpya,, v.l. mānatva (so Index; ed. mānātva), but mānāpya without v.l.; Tib. renders mgu bar bya ba, making glad (= ārādhanā); Chin. respectful behavior; this accords with the Pali comm. () on the passage (, bhikkhunā … bhikkhu-mānattāya paṭipajjitabbaṃ, ciṇṇamānatto bhikkhu …) corresponding to above; the comm. says, bhikkhu-mānattāyā ti bhikkhūnaṃ mānanabhāvāya, ārādhanatthāyā (cf. on Tib. above) ti vuttaṃ hoti; it thus appears that, according to both northern and southern tradition, this penance consisted in, or at least involved, some kind of ceremonial homage paid by the culprit to the general community of monks. This can be interpreted as supporting the apparent etym., māna-tva, condition of (paying) respect.
